WORKLOG / TEST DOSSIER — task 0 (country_home_loan_servicing), revision 2 after the policy-task audit.

[Step 0 — draw and scope] draw_counts.py --task 0 printed: {"task": 0, "key": "env_0053_agricultural_lending_cooperative/country_home_loan_servicing/0", "prerequisite_problems": 3, "problems": 4, "factor_counts": [5, 4, 4, 4]}. Root homeloan_ext_escrow_shortage_paid_at_once takes 5 factors; homeloan_ext_late_charge_reopened_month, homeloan_ext_returned_remittance_fee and homeloan_ext_replacement_remittance take 4 each. Task 0 occupies these four policies and their tools assess_late_charge_eed44226, assess_returned_item_fee_25e49e31, apply_replacement_remittance_c604a214, pay_escrow_shortage_8ff65e44 (returned payment, late charge, escrow shortage). Task 1 keeps the disjoint pair escrow waiver / member paydown.

[Why it is a good test] The member asks only to pay her escrow shortage at once. The shortage is fixed only once no monthly payment stands unpaid, and her October 2026 autopay remittance came back for insufficient funds without her knowing. Replacing it waits on the late charge and returned-payment fee the return caused, which the ledger does not carry. So the agent reads three rules she never mentions, finds each waited-on state false in the records and books four writes in order, each with its own arithmetic. Each problem has exactly one tool; the difficulty is reading and computing.

[Problem-tree card]
 (1) root A <- P (homeloan_ext_replacement_remittance), value_input, gate bal, state form: "The shortage paid at once is fixed only after no monthly payment on the loan stands unpaid past its due date." Ordering connective 'only after'; waits on a record-visible state; no tool, id or code token; hard, all monthly payments. Only the replacement pays a monthly bill in this difficulty. False at opening: bill 111403c1 (due 2026-10-01) reversed by the nsf return, accrued_interest 676.36, escrow_balance 2753.00. Skipping the edge gives 1020.48 instead of 418.66.
 (2) P <- L (late charge), value_input, gate fees_owed, state form, negated direction: "A replacement remittance is not figured until the ledger carries a late charge for every reopened monthly payment whose grace period has ended." Only the late-charge write books a late charge. False at opening: no late charge points to the October bill; grace ended 2026-10-16. Skipping gives 1770.67 instead of 1779.50.
 (3) P <- Q (returned-payment fee), value_input, gate fees_owed, state form: "A replacement remittance is figured only after the ledger carries a returned-payment fee for every returned remittance whose return reason calls for one." Only the returned-fee write books one. False at opening: no fee points to the October return 3a2e8a4c. Skipping gives 1758.80.
 Three value_input edges (floor 2). Order L, Q, P, A; L and Q commute. The user write is A (the member's one-time debit of her own account).

[Base-invariant card] L and Q write homeloan_fee_assessed: homeloan_evt_late_charge gates homeloan_late_after_grace (due date as day 0, more than 15 days, exclusive: 2026-10-16 no charge, 2026-10-17 it arises; frozen 2026-10-20) and homeloan_one_late_charge, plus policy_scope for the returned-payment, escrow waiver, mortgage insurance, recast and insurance rules. P writes payments, a monthly escrow deposit and fee payments: homeloan_accepts_payments (status active) and escrow analysis policy_scope. A writes a shortage_lump_sum deposit: both governing rules policy_scope.

[Business-object card] Loan 0fa5aeeb (Country Home 30-Year Fixed). Reopened object: bill 111403c1 with reversed interest 76236656 (676.36), principal 3a2e8a4c (466.32), escrow 271664f3 (601.82), all carrying channel autopay. Earlier returns: December 2025 (return 4c7ea509-cc45-48a7-8b16-c4b17b5a90f6, fee d9ef152b-6e54-4987-995f-3ffea0a181cb 18.00, late charge 7370fa25-c754-4c8b-b8bc-525239944abc 10.47 waived as a courtesy on 2025-12-22) and March 2026 (return b8152c4d, fee fa17ba67 24.00, late charge 6328ce52 10.47), both replaced and their fees settled; the farm loan's 2026-03-01 autopay installment was returned and replaced on 2026-03-06. fees_due at opening 0.00.

[Factor card — L, late charge 14.30] charge_measure (method, date): opened 2019-10-18, on or after 2016-01-01 and before 2021-01-01, so the association's installment note measures the charge on the whole monthly installment on record, 1156.80 + 630.39 = 1787.19; baseline (the principal-and-interest payment alone) gives 12.50 after the floor; near-miss: a loan opened from 2021 would be measured on 1156.80 alone, one opened before 2016 would carry the flat 25.00. late_rate (parameter, history): two late charges in the twelve months less one late charge waiver (the December courtesy) leaves one counting, 4.0%; baseline 5% gives 17.87. relationship_relief (parameter, cross-difficulty farmland, multi-source): active FarmLand loan, principal installments paid 2025-03-01 and 2026-03-06 (the 2026-03-01 debit was returned and does not count), no farm late charge, 80%; baseline 0 gives 71.49. charge_floor (parameter): 84 months with one counting, 12.50; baseline 15.00. Whole baseline 57.84.
[Factor card — Q, returned fee 26.17] returns_counted (method, cross-difficulty farmland): the return carries channel autopay and the farm loan also pays by automatic debit, so returns on both loans in 12 months count: home December and March, farm March, 3; baseline (home only, 2) gives 24.00. returned_fee_by_count (parameter): nsf with three others, 45.00; baseline 30.00 gives 18.00. returned_item_limit (parameter): returned 1744.50, 2.5% = 43.61; baseline none gives 27.00. member_owner_relief (parameter, cross-difficulty equity, multi-source): Class B active, patronage 2026-03-13, 40%; baseline 0 gives 43.61. Whole baseline 30.00.
[Factor card — P, replacement 1779.50] pi_share_carried (parameter): the October bill was billed at 3.875 and the note rate on record is 4.000 (autopay discount removed 2026-10-09, payment re-amortised to 1156.80), so the reversed 1142.68; baseline 1156.80 gives 1793.62. escrow_share_carried (parameter): analysis 2026-10-05 later than the 2026-10-01 due date, so the reversed 601.82; baseline 630.39 gives 1808.07. fees_carried (method): nsf and a repeat return in 12 months, so every unpaid fee 40.47; baseline no fee gives 1744.50. fee_carry_limit (parameter, cross-difficulty farmland, multi-source): 35.00; baseline no limit gives 1784.97. Whole baseline 1787.19. After the write fees_due 5.47 stays (beyond the limit).
[Factor card — A, shortage 418.66] tax_growth_allowance (parameter): 4061.27 against 3812.40 paid 12-24 months ago (+6.53%), 6%, 4304.95; baseline 134.36. insurance_renewal_allowance (parameter): 1778.00 against 1684.00 (+5.58%), 4%, 1849.12; baseline 335.68. insurance_due_month (method): expiry on record 2027-06-15 is projection month 7, so May 2027 (month 6) instead of the February anniversary; baseline 905.27. mortgage_insurance_months (method): scheduled 78% (204360.00) reached on payment 93 (2027-08-01), 9 months of 143.78; baseline 706.22. cushion_base (method): MI in force and projected 9 months, cushion on tax and homeowner's 6154.07, 1025.68; baseline 634.33. Whole baseline 825.56 = the member's 2026-10-05 letter figure (the standard analysis on the same balance).

[Seed] Monthly bills, autopay payments and escrow deposits 2025-01 to 2026-10 (deposit 581.88 to 2025-10, 601.82 from 2025-11; the analysis of 2026-10-05 set 630.39 for the year from 2026-11), the December 2025, March 2026 and October 2026 returns with reversal rows carrying the autopay channel, the earlier fees and replacements, the courtesy waiver, monthly MI disbursements, two tax and two homeowner's bills; the farm loan on automatic debit with 2024-2026 installments and its March 2026 return, fee and replacement; Class B stock with 2025 and 2026 cash patronage. Every earlier fee follows the same rules (see seed_consistency). Ledger rows before 2025-01 are not loaded; balances on the loan row are the official running totals. No other clause fires: 19 days past due (no nonaccrual), no other bill past grace, MI auto-termination scheduled 2027-08-01.

[Persona] Renata volunteers the goal and her letter's 825.56; credentials, account, insurance and earlier bounces only when asked; she reacts to the October return only after the agent raises it; approves the debit for the amount given; questions a figure that differs from her letter once, then accepts.

[Standard solution and verification] Reads: find_customers (phone), verify (phone + member number), find_homeloan_loans, find_homeloan_transactions, find_homeloan_escrow, find_farmland_loans, find_farmland_transactions, find_equity_accounts, find_equity_transactions. Writes: late charge 14.30 on bill 111403c1; returned fee 26.17 on return 3a2e8a4c; replacement 1779.50 on bill 111403c1 (pays the late charge 14.30 and 20.70 of the returned fee); the member's shortage debit 418.66. Recomputed by replaying the real tools to each step and evaluating the policy compute (the check_compute engine): L 14.30 (12.50 / 17.87 / 71.49 / 15.00, baseline 57.84); Q 26.17 (24.00 / 18.00 / 27.00 / 43.61, baseline 30.00); P 1779.50 (1793.62 / 1808.07 / 1744.50 / 1784.97, baseline 1787.19); A 418.66 (134.36 / 335.68 / 905.27 / 706.22 / 634.33, baseline 825.56). Edge skips: A without P 1020.48; P without L 1770.67; P without Q 1758.80.

[Draft recomputation from the visible context] The shortage rule waits on no payment unpaid; the history shows October reversed; the replacement rule waits on a late charge for every reopened month past grace and a returned fee for every return that calls for one; neither exists. The late-charge rule reads the waiver history, the late-charge count, the payment on record, the farm loan and the loan's age; the returned-fee rule reads the return channel, the farm loan's autopay and returns, the size of the return and the equity record; the replacement rule reads the bill's rate, the analysis date, the return count and the farm loan; the shortage rule reads the tax and homeowner's bills, the expiry on record, the original amortization and MI status. The same four writes and figures as gold.

[Revisions] r1 and r2 (first round): March late charge seeded so the late-charge history bears weight; deposit 630.39 aligned with the standard analysis. r3 (audit round 2): F-2/F-5 the late charge no longer selects a measured payment (it is measured on the payment on record) and gained an honest method, the courtesy fresh-start count (superseded, see r6); F-7 the relief rule now names the case of an active farm loan with fewer than two paid installments; F-1/F-8 the returned-fee look-back by window length was replaced by a counting method (relationship-wide for autopay members whose farm loan is also on autopay; for a one-time payment, the other one-time payments returned on the home loan; home loan otherwise), and return entries now carry the remittance's channel; F-3 the replacement's fee ladder now turns on return reason and repeat returns, so its fall-through (an unauthorized return) is reachable; F-4 the replacement's P&I share now turns on the billed rate and the final payment, its forbearance tier removed; F-11..F-14 the shortage rule's due-month range, cushion-base tiers, earlier-bill definition (12 to 24 months ago) and payment-number definition were aligned with compute; T0-F5 the edge figures were recomputed. The seed was re-figured accordingly: the August 2025 return was replaced by a December 2025 return whose late charge was forgiven as a courtesy, the March fees re-figured (24.00, 10.28 paid in full; both seeded late charges are 10.47 since r6), the farm loan put on automatic debit with a returned March 2026 installment, and a 2024 farm installment added. Values moved: L 13.71 -> 13.88, Q 23.03 -> 26.17, P 1769.50 -> 1779.50; A unchanged 418.66.

[Revisions r4 — audit round 3] R2-T0-F1 / N-1: the late-charge count ladder's error-correction tier collapsed into its fall-through; the error-correction exclusion was made common to every tier and the second tier was anchored on an approved forbearance (both superseded in round 4, and the count ladder itself removed in round 5, see r6). R2-T0-F2 / N-2 and N-2b: the returned-fee count for a one-time payment no longer uses late charges as a proxy; it counts the other one-time payments returned on the home loan, a record set no other write of this tree touches, so the late charge and returned fee commute on every world. N-3: farm installments paid are now principal payments less principal returns in 24 months (here 2, the returned 2026-03-01 debit not counting). F-13: the shortage rule now says the property tax and the homeowner's premium are each projected as one bill at the latest bill, as computed. F-14 / N-5: the payment number of a due date is now the amortization months less the whole months to maturity (here 360 - 276 = 84), which is how a servicer numbers payments whatever the closing day. No scored value moved: L 13.88, Q 26.17, P 1779.50, A 418.66; every sensitivity and baseline is unchanged.

[Revisions r5 — audit round 4] R3-T0-F1 / R3-N1: the late-charge count's tiers no longer differ only in where a window starts; every tier counts the same twelve months and the tiers are different counting rules over different record sets: a courtesy-waived member has the courtesy waivers taken off as well as the error corrections (the courtesy strikes the charge from the record), a member with an active farm real estate loan and no courtesy has the farm loan's late charges of the twelve months added (the cooperative weighs the whole repayment record), anyone else counts the home loan's late charges less error corrections (the baseline). On this world the courtesy tier gave 2 - 0 - 1 = 1. (This ladder was found to repeat the fall-through in round 4 and is removed, see r6.) R3-N2: the error-correction and courtesy subtractions now count only late charge waivers (fee_code late_charge), and the rule now says they are the waivers recorded in the twelve months, as computed. No scored value moved: L 13.88, Q 26.17, P 1779.50, A 418.66; every sensitivity and baseline is unchanged.

[Revisions r6 — audit round 5] R4-T0-F1 / R4-N1: no honest three-way counting method survives the test that each tier's rule must differ from the fall-through's on the fall-through's own worlds (a subtract-if-any or add-if-any tier always collapses there), so the count ladder repeat_count_basis was removed. The count is now one rule (late charges in the twelve months less the late charge waivers recorded in them, error correction or courtesy alike), read by late_rate, and the method moved to a real servicing distinction: the note the loan was closed on fixes how the late charge is measured. charge_measure (method, date): a loan opened from 2021-01-01 is on the uniform secondary-market note (the late charge rate times the principal-and-interest payment, the baseline); one opened 2016-01-01 to 2020-12-31 is on the association's installment note (the rate times the whole monthly installment, principal and interest plus escrow deposit; the rule now supersedes the base clause that kept the escrow part out of the charge); one opened before 2016 is on the former rural residence note (a flat 25.00 whatever the rate). (In r6 the ladder listed the uniform note first and the flat pre-2016 charge as its fall-through; r7 reordered it so the fall-through is the uniform note, which is the baseline; the paper check is restated in r7.) relief_full_pct rose from 70 to 80 so every factor of this charge still bears weight on this world (at 70% the 21.45 result would sit above both floors). The two seeded late charges were refigured under the same rule, 10.28 -> 10.47 (3% of 1744.50, less 80%), with the courtesy waiver and the March fee payment. R4-O1 is moot: the farm late charges no longer enter the count. Values moved: L 13.88 -> 14.30; fees after the replacement 5.05 -> 5.47; the replacement's no-limit baseline 1784.55 -> 1784.97 and the edge skip P without Q 1758.38 -> 1758.80; Q 26.17, P 1779.50 and A 418.66 unchanged.

[Revisions r7 — audit round 6] R5-T0-F1 / R5-N1: charge_measure's fall-through is now its baseline. The ladder runs: opened before legacy_note_before (2016-01-01), the former rural residence note, a flat legacy_flat_charge_usd; opened from 2016-01-01 to before uniform_note_from (2021-01-01), the association's installment note, the late charge rate times the whole monthly installment on record; otherwise (opened from 2021-01-01), the uniform secondary-market note, the rate times the principal-and-interest payment on record, which is the baseline and what the computation document states. The rule sentence lists the notes in the same order, and the compute tests the flat tier first and the uniform note last. The tiers, their conditions and this world's tier (the installment note, opened 2019-10-18) are unchanged, so no value moved: L 14.30 (12.50 / 17.87 / 71.49 / 15.00, baseline 57.84), Q 26.17, P 1779.50, A 418.66. Paper check on the fall-through's own worlds (loans opened from 2021): the flat tier gives 25.00 whatever the payment and the rate, against the rate times the payment; the installment tier gives the rate times the payment plus the escrow deposit, so it differs by the rate share of the deposit; the two meet only on a loan that collects no escrow deposit at all (an escrow-waived loan, whose whole installment is its principal-and-interest payment), which is a fact of that loan and not of the tier's condition, the way the returned fee's relationship tier meets its home-loan tier on a member whose farm loan had no return. No two tiers differ only in a number or a window. Every other factor of the charter was re-checked for the same property (fall-through tier = baseline): all already held except the returned-payment fee's ladder in the returned-fee rule, whose fall-through named the product's fee while its baseline also carried the base rule's 'none when unauthorized'; its separate unauthorized tier was folded into the fall-through, whose value is now literally the baseline (0 if the return reason is unauthorized, else returned_payment_fee_usd). Compute and this world's tier (nsf with three others, 45.00) are unchanged. R5-O1 (the installment note measures today's installment on record, 1156.80 + 630.39, not the reopened October installment, 1142.68 + 601.82): left as the auditor's realism observation. The rule names the record's figures, as the base rule names monthly_pi_amount, so there is one reading. Measuring the October installment instead would need a second sub-rule for months with no returned remittance, and it would put this world's late-rate baseline on a half-cent tie (1744.50 x 5% x 20% = 17.445).
user_scenario: You are Renata K. Sobotka, fifty-two, who runs a small cow-calf herd on the family ground west of Ord, Nebraska, and lives in the house on the acreage at 47215 Mira Valley Road. You are practical, friendly enough, and short on patience for paperwork; you talk plainly and do not volunteer more than you are asked. You are calling the Cottonwood Plains Farm Credit servicing desk about the escrow analysis letter for your house loan dated October 5. The letter says your escrow account is short and shows a higher monthly payment starting in November if the shortage is spread out over the year. You would much rather pay the whole shortage now, in one go, out of your checking account, so the monthly house payment does not go up. That is what you want done today; you are glad for the agent to set it up, and you understand you will have to approve that debit yourself when they send it to you. From the letter you remember only that it put the shortage at $825.56. When the agent asks who you are, give your phone number, 4024647316. If they want one more thing, read your member number off a patronage notice: CPF-4371958. Only if they ask for something else do you give the last four of your Social Security number, 7124, or your email, renata.sobotka@ordwireless.net. If they ask which account the money should come from, it is your checking at Ord Community Credit Union, account ending 4419. If they ask about your homeowner's insurance, you moved it to Sandhills Mutual in June, the new policy runs to June 15, 2027, and you paid that first year yourself. If they ask whether you would rather spread the shortage out, the answer is no. If the agent asks about earlier bounced payments, you admit money was tight last winter: the December and March house payments came back too, and the farm loan's March payment, and you asked for the December late fee to be forgiven and it was. If the agent tells you that your October house payment came back unpaid from the bank, you are surprised: you moved your checking to the credit union at the start of October and phoned on the 9th to stop the automatic withdrawals from the old account, and you assumed October had already gone through. Once the agent explains what it takes to put October right, tell them to go ahead and take that payment now, by phone, from your credit union checking; you accept the amount they give you and do not argue about it. When the agent tells you how much the shortage is and hands you the payment to approve, approve it for exactly the amount the agent gave you. If that amount is not the $825.56 your letter shows, say so and ask them to make sure; if they stand by their figure, go along with it. Once you have approved the shortage payment and seen that it went through, thank them and end the call.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: The replacement remittance has two parallel prerequisites, the late charge and the returned-payment fee. They commute: each books one fee assessment row and adds its own amount to fees_due, and neither formula reads the other's row (the late charge reads the late-charge and waiver counts, the opening date, the payment and escrow deposit on record and the farm ledger; the returned fee reads the return rows, the farm loan's autopay and returns and the equity ledger). Booking the returned fee first gives the same two rows, fees_due 40.47 and the same replacement 1779.50; the replacement then pays the fees in assessment order, the same-day tie broken by reference number, which is the same in both orders, so the late charge 14.30 is paid in full and 20.70 of the returned fee, leaving 5.47. The chain fees before replacement, replacement before shortage, is pinned by the two prerequisite sentences of the replacement rule and the one of the shortage rule.
